Answer questions from the passage below:
Arms control regulates the acquisition or development of weapons. The
Anti-ballistic Missile (ABM) Treaty in 1972 tried to stop the United States
and Soviet Union from using ballistic missiles as a defensive shield to
launch a nuclear attack. While it did allow both countries to deploy a very
limited number of defensive systems, it stopped them from large-scale
production of those systems. The US and Soviet Union signed a number of
other arms control treaties, including the Strategic Arms Limitations Treaty
II or SALT II and the Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty (START). The Nuclear
Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) of 1968 was an arms control treaty in the
sense that it regulated the acquisition of nuclear weapons: those countries
that had tested and manufactured nuclear weapons before 1967 were
allowed to keep their weapons; and those that had not done so were to
give up the right to acquire them. The NPT did not abolish nuclear
weapons: rather, it limited the number of countries that could have them.
Which among the following statement is correct about NPT?

It froze the nuclear club to the five countries that had manufactured and exploded a nuclear weapon prior to 1 January 1967, requiring all other signatory states to forgo acquiring nuclear capability.
Hence, option (B) is correct.

questionText:
Match List I (Leader) with List II (Country / Historical Role):

List I:
(A) Sheikh Mujibur Rahman
(B) Zulfikar Ali Bhutto
(C) Velupillai Prabhakaran
(D) Mohamed Nasheed

List II:
(I) Founding Father of Bangladesh and Awami League leader
(II) Elected Prime Minister of Pakistan who signed Simla Agreement
(III) Supreme commander of the militant LTTE in Sri Lanka
(IV) First democratically elected multi-party President of Maldives

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.
Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Sheikh Mujib led Bangladesh to independence; Z.A. Bhutto led Pakistan after 1971; Prabhakaran led the LTTE; Mohamed Nasheed was elected Maldivian President in 2008.
Hence, Option C is correct.
Hence, option (A) is the correct match.

chapter: South Asia in the Post-Cold War Era
questionText:
Arrange the following developments in South Asia in the correct
chronological order.
 
(A) India and Sri Lanka signed the Free Trade Agreement.
(B) Vajpayee-Musharraf Agra Summit.
(C) Six point proposal of Sheikh Mujib-ur Rahman for greater autonomy to
East Pakistan.
(D) India and Pakistan sign an agreement not to attack nuclear installations
of each other.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.
Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Chronology of South Asian developments: (C) Sheikh Mujibur Rahman proposed his 6-point demand for East Pakistani autonomy in 1966; (D) India and Pakistan signed the agreement on non-attack of nuclear facilities in December 1988; (A) India and Sri Lanka signed the Free Trade Agreement in December 1998; (B) Prime Minister Vajpayee and President Pervez Musharraf held the Agra Summit in July 2001. Sequence: (C), (D), (A), (B).
Hence, option (A) is correct.

questionText:
Arrange the following events in the chronological sequence of occurrence–
 
(A) Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty
(B) The Antarctic Treaty
(C) Chemical Weapons Convention
(D) Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty
 
Choose the correct answer from the following options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Chronology of international disarmament and conservation treaties:
1. (B) The Antarctic Treaty: Signed in 1959, prohibiting military bases and weapons testing.
2. (D) Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT): Opened for signature in 1968.
3. (A) Anti-Ballistic Missile (ABM) Treaty: Signed in 1972 between the US and the USSR.
4. (C) Chemical Weapons Convention (CWC): Signed in Paris in January 1993, banning chemical weapons.
Sequence: (B), (D), (A), (C).
Hence, option (B) is correct.
